templates.name: Firewall-Router (Example Music)
templates.description:
2026-10-25 CORRECTION to the note immediately below, same day: the cross-template DEPENDENT-item fix described there (master_item pointing at linuxtools_examplemusic's own vfs.file.contents[...] item, with a "templates" parent-link entry) was REJECTED live by configuration.import: "Cannot link template 'linuxtools_examplemusic' to template 'firewall_examplemusic', because it would be linked to host 'EXAFWLCLD001' twice." Confirmed against real Zabbix community reports of the identical error class (forum: "cannot link template because its parent template would be linked twice"; ZBX-9842: "template cannot be linked to another template more than once even through other templates") -- this is a hard Zabbix constraint on the host's own template graph, not an import-tooling quirk, and it fires precisely BECAUSE every host here gets linuxtools_examplemusic linked directly regardless of role, which is the whole point of the template design. This ALSO means bind9/tacticalrmm's own identical "templates" parent-link pattern (referenced below) would hit the exact same wall the first time either is actually linked to a real host alongside linuxtools_examplemusic -- flagged separately, not yet fixed on those two. REPLACED with the fix described in the next paragraph: an independently-keyed local master item, no parent-link, no host-linking conflict.

2026-10-25 ACTUAL FIX (supersedes the parent-link approach above): added this template's own vfs.file.contents[/etc/example-music/nodeinfo.json,UTF-8] master item (see its own description for why the UTF-8 param exists) and repointed all 9 firewall-specific dependent items at it instead of linuxtools' item. Same file, read independently by each template that needs its own extras -- no cross-template reference, no parent-link, no collision (confirmed: distinct key string from linuxtools' own bare-key item). NOT YET VERIFIED against a real re-import.

2026-10-25 BUG FIX, Robert, live on EXAFWLCLD001: all 9 firewall-specific nodeinfo fields (lan_ip/lan_iface/ansible_ip/wg_role/wg_tunnel_ip/wg_hub/wan_iface/wan_mode/wan_ip) were returning no data despite the real file having correct values. Root cause: the original master item was a vfs.file.regexp expecting those 9 keys to appear consecutively in one exact literal order (firewallme.sh's own bash/jq field order). Ansible's ansible.builtin.copy + to_nice_json (used by every Ansible-side nodeinfo write, incl. linux/tools.yml which runs against every host on every re-run) always re-serializes the file with keys sorted ALPHABETICALLY, so that literal-order assumption never matched the real on-disk file. Fixed by switching to the same proven cross-template DEPENDENT-item pattern already live on templates 6/7 (bind9/tacticalrmm, see feedback_zabbix_duplicate_item_keys_across_templates.md): each of the 9 items now points its master_item at linuxtools_examplemusic's own vfs.file.contents[/etc/example-music/nodeinfo.json] item (real JSONPATH against real JSON, immune to key order) instead of redeclaring a home-grown regex master item of its own. Added the top-level "templates" parent-link entry this cross-template reference needs at import time. NOT YET VERIFIED against a real re-import -- same caveat bind9/tacticalrmm's own fix still carries.

Companion template for bootstrap/web/provision/firewallme.sh + ansible/playbooks/firewallme -- built by copying zabbix_template_ansible.json's generator and editing it. Same flat, native, one-item-per-thing design.

DELIBERATELY NOT CHECKED (Robert's explicit calls, 2026-10-17)
  - cockpit-navigator: a one-off GitHub .deb, not an apt package -- no stable copyright path. Revisit next week.
  - /home/ansible/.zshrc, /root/.zshrc, ansible user's shell=zsh: already covered by linuxtools' template (linked to every Linux node, firewalls included) -- not duplicated here.
  - /etc/cockpit/cockpit.conf, /etc/cockpit/ws-certs.d/0-self-signed.cert: skipped for now.
  - /etc/wireguard/{private,public,preshared}.key and wg0.conf: NOT checked. The directory itself is mode 0700 (both firewallme.sh and the Ansible role set this) -- the zabbix-agent user has no search permission into it at all, so this isn't just the usual 'can't read file contents' caveat, nothing inside this directory is even stat-able.
  - nftables RULESET CONTENT: not checked. Role- and site-conditional (WAN SSH, WireGuard port, CLD-only rules) -- Robert's call: 'too much can go wrong, this is an advanced thing.' Only the file's existence is checked.
  - wg0.conf peer registration (which spokes are actually registered on their hub) and the whole hub/spoke role-aware design: deferred, backlog.
  - /etc/resolv.conf: written chattr +i (immutable) by the role -- a plain vfs.file.exists can't see that attribute, and existence alone is nearly always true anyway. Backlogged, not built.
  - root's shell=zsh on a firewall host: not covered by linuxtools (that template's root-shell check is the ansible-control-node-specific one, a different host) -- backlogged, not built here either.

DESIGN NOTES
  - Package list is fw_packages minus the 11 packages already in common_packages (computed programmatically, not by hand) -- linuxtools' template already covers those on every Linux node.
  - /etc/dnsmasq.d/lan.conf and NetworkManager.conf's managed=false check are both INVERTED (trigger fires on the bad state being PRESENT, not absent) -- a legacy file that should be gone, and a line that should have been corrected away.
  - PasswordAuthentication/ChallengeResponseAuthentication check the directive EXISTS, not which value it has -- fw_ssh_password_auth_enabled is a genuine per-host policy choice (default true), not a single correct value to assert estate-wide.
  - Service checks use systemctl is-enabled via system.run (AllowKey=system.run[*] already in every deployed agent config) rather than 'is it running' -- several services are legitimately enabled-but-not-started when fw_wan_activate=false (a fresh, not-yet-activated box). Also used for the /etc/network/interfaces ifupdown-stanza check -- the real WAN/LAN interface names are detected per-host at runtime, not a fixed literal a static template item can know, but grep -v on the literal string 'lo' needs no such knowledge.
  - nodeinfo.json's 9 firewall-specific fields (lan_ip/lan_iface/ansible_ip/wg_role/wg_tunnel_ip/wg_hub/wan_iface/wan_mode/wan_ip, 90-firewall.yml's own nodeinfo_extra) ARE extracted here -- added 2026-10-17 once ansible/tasks/nodeinfo.yml's extras-preservation fix (32e288f) landed, confirming WireGuard/firewall-specific nodeinfo fields belong in THIS template, not linuxtools' generic one (Robert's explicit design call).

items.name: File exists: /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/wan.nmconnection
items.description: 1 if /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/wan.nmconnection exists (WAN NM profile). CAVEAT: this directory is likely mode 0700 (NetworkManager's own convention, protecting any Wi-Fi PSKs in other profiles) -- the zabbix-agent user may be unable to even stat this file, in which case the item goes unsupported rather than showing a reliable 0. Not live-verified.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} is missing /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/wan.nmconnection
triggers.description: Re-run the firewall role. If this item is permanently unsupported (not 0/1), it's the directory-permission caveat above, not a real fault -- check manually.

items.name: Legacy /etc/dnsmasq.d/lan.conf still present
items.description: 1 if the legacy pre-Ansible-port lan.conf still exists. It should have been removed by 08_dnsmasq.yml (superseded by exa-firewall.conf) -- its continued presence causes real config drift, since dnsmasq loads /etc/dnsmasq.d/*.conf alphabetically and lan.conf's unprefixed domain-name directive loads AFTER and overrides exa-firewall.conf's correct one.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} still has legacy /etc/dnsmasq.d/lan.conf -- remove it
triggers.description: Remove /etc/dnsmasq.d/lan.conf -- it is superseded by exa-firewall.conf and causes real DHCP/DNS config drift if left in place. Safe to delete; the role never re-creates it.

items.name: /etc/network/interfaces non-lo stanza count
items.description: Count of auto/iface/allow-* lines in /etc/network/interfaces NOT mentioning lo -- should be 0, since the role strips any ifupdown stanza for the WAN/LAN interfaces (their real names are detected per-host at runtime, not a fixed literal this check can name). items.name: nodeinfo.json contents, firewall extras (master)
items.description: Raw nodeinfo.json content -- master item for this template's own 9 firewall-specific examplemusic.nodeinfo.* dependent items below. Deliberately a SEPARATE item from linuxtools_examplemusic's own vfs.file.contents[/etc/example-music/nodeinfo.json] master (same file, read twice -- negligible cost, a local file read), NOT a cross-template DEPENDENT reference to it. 2026-10-25 real finding: Zabbix refuses to link a template declaring another template as a parent (the "templates" field, needed to resolve a cross-template master_itemid) to any host that ALSO links that parent template directly -- "cannot link template ... because it would be linked to host ... twice" -- and every host here gets linuxtools_examplemusic directly regardless of role. The UTF-8 encoding param exists purely to give this item a distinct key from linuxtools' own bare-key item (both read the identical file independently) -- real file content either way, no functional difference, avoids the duplicate-key collision the template-1-5 backlog item already warns about (feedback_zabbix_duplicate_item_keys_across_templates.md). No staleness trigger of its own -- linuxtools' own master item's nodata() trigger already covers this same file going stale, one alert, not duplicated here.
